entries.name: U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland
entries.summary: Visitors may not bring smart glasses into the courthouse, with limited exceptions.

source.publisher: U.S. District Court, District of Maryland

entries.name: Polk County Public Schools
entries.summary: Students may not possess or wear Meta/Ray-Ban smart glasses and similar wearable recording or communication devices in school.

entries.name: New York State Unified Court System (all state and local courts)
entries.summary: Smart glasses are prohibited in the state's courthouses.

source.publisher: New York State Unified Court System

entries.name: Philadelphia First Judicial District courthouses
entries.summary: Glasses with any recording capability, prescription included, are not permitted in any First Judicial District courthouse, building or office without written authorization; wearers are denied entry.

entries.name: Marine Corps Installations East (MCB Camp Lejeune)
entries.summary: Smart glasses are prohibited for use and wear aboard MCIEAST-MCB Camp Lejeune under the region's photo and video policy.

entries.name: U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin
entries.summary: Smart glasses are on the court's list of prohibited items.

source.publisher: U.S. District Court, Western District of Wisconsin

entries.name: U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida
entries.summary: Smart glasses are prohibited in all areas of the courthouse.

source.publisher: U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida

entries.name: SAT test centers (College Board)
entries.summary: Smart glasses and any eyewear with internet or AI features are not allowed during testing, prescription pairs included.

entries.summary: Smart glasses may come aboard but may not be used in the casino, spa, restrooms, locker rooms, medical areas, youth areas or crew areas.

entries.name: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement workplaces
entries.summary: An internal memo (reported, not public) bars employees from wearing Meta's glasses in the federal workspace.

entries.name: Courts and tribunals of England and Wales (HMCTS)
entries.summary: Meta's glasses are prohibited in criminal, civil and family courts and tribunals in England and Wales; they are taken at the entrance and returned on exit.

entries.name: GCSE and A level exam rooms (JCQ)
entries.summary: Smart glasses are unauthorised material that candidates must not take into the exam room; possession alone can lead to sanctions.

entries.name: ATG Theatres (UK)
entries.summary: Reported to ask wearers to remove camera glasses (at ATG, during performances).

entries.name: Soho House (UK)
entries.summary: Reported to ask wearers to remove camera glasses (at ATG, during performances).

entries.name: Jeremy King restaurants (London)
entries.summary: Reported to ask wearers to remove camera glasses (at ATG, during performances).

entries.name: UK Comic-Con (Monopoly Events)
entries.summary: Attendees may not wear any recording device at its events; offenders may be removed.

entries.name: Senedd Siambr (Welsh Parliament debating chamber)
entries.summary: Members may not use smart glasses in the Siambr until a review is complete (temporary).
entries.lifecycle_note: Applies until a review is complete; no end date published.

entries.name: Western Australia public schools
entries.summary: Smart glasses are banned on government school premises and at school events for students, staff, parents, visitors and contractors (exemptions for approved medical/accessibility reasons).

entries.name: City of Sydney pools
entries.summary: Smart glasses may not be used at City of Sydney pools; the resolution extends the rule to leisure centres, libraries and childcare.

entries.name: Yarra City Council pools, gyms, playgrounds and childcare
entries.summary: Smart glasses barred from council pools, gyms, playgrounds and childcare.

entries.name: Brisbane City Council public pools
entries.summary: Bans filming people without consent at its public pools. Wearing the glasses is still allowed.

entries.name: Early childhood education and care services (Australia, staff)
entries.summary: Staff cannot use or carry personal devices, smart glasses included, while working directly with children.

entries.name: Victoria schools (students)
entries.summary: Students at every Victorian school must keep smart glasses switched off and stored during school hours (Ministerial Order No. 1515).

entries.name: Victoria government schools (adults and visitors)
entries.summary: Nobody, parents and visitors included, may wear or use smart glasses on government school premises or at school events.

entries.name: City of Canterbury Bankstown leisure and aquatic centres
entries.summary: Council voted to ban smart glasses from all its leisure and aquatic facilities; conditions of entry not yet updated as of Nov 15, 2026 per VR.org.
entries.lifecycle_note: Voted 2026-09-15; conditions of entry not yet updated (per VR.org, 2026-11-15).

entries.name: Oslo municipal schools
entries.summary: AI glasses are not allowed during the school day ("KI-briller er ikke tillatt i skoletiden").

entries.name: Punjab province (Pakistan)
entries.summary: Section 144 order bans wearing, using and selling camera glasses with hidden recording ability (and disguised mini cameras) across Punjab. First 30-day order 2026-10-20; extended for another 30 days (reported 2026-11-19).
entries.lifecycle_note: First 30-day order from 2026-10-20 (Dawn). Extension order issued 2026-11-19 under s.144 CrPC for 30 days, effective immediately, unless withdrawn earlier (Dunya News 2026-11-19; Express Tribune and Pakistan Observer 2026-11-20). Counting 30 days from 19 Nov gives a last day of 18 Dec 2026; the notification text itself was not found online, so the end date is derived, not published. Found by the refresher flagging the first expiry.

entries.name: Canadian Department of National Defence / CAF secure zones
entries.summary: AI glasses are forbidden in all Operations, Security and High Security Zones.

entries.name: CSAT exam rooms (South Korea)
entries.summary: Having smart glasses in the exam room voids that year's exam; wearing them also bars the student from the next year's test.

entries.name: Courts Service of Ireland (court buildings)

entries.name: United States (recreational drone rules)
entries.summary: Recreational flyers: in controlled airspace (Class B, C, D and surface Class E around airports) only with prior FAA authorization via LAANC or DroneZone; at or below 400 ft in Class G.

entries.name: Canada (where to fly a drone)
entries.summary: Unless following an established Transport Canada procedure, do not fly closer than 5.6 km (3 NM) to certified airports or 1.9 km (1 NM) to certified heliports; within 3 NM of a National Defence aerodrome you need its authorization.

entries.name: Australia (flying drones near airports)
entries.summary: Drones over 250 g must not fly within 5.5 km of a controlled airport or in runway approach/departure paths (up to 7 km); 250 g or less may fly up to 45 m within 5.5 km but not over approach paths or inside the airport boundary.

entries.name: European Union (EASA open category)
entries.summary: Low-risk 'open category' drone flights in EASA states are limited to 120 m height, with subcategory rules (A1/A2/A3) on flying over or near uninvolved people; national geographical zones add local restrictions.

entries.name: AP Exams (College Board)
entries.summary: Students must not bring electronic equipment, including wearable technology of any kind, smart glasses, smartwatches, recording devices or cameras; anyone seen with one during testing or breaks may be dismissed and have the score cancelled.

entries.name: New Zealand (drones near aerodromes)
entries.summary: Within 4 km of any aerodrome you need an appropriate qualification (or direct supervision) and must not fly over runway strips; you also need the aerodrome operator's consent and, in controlled airspace, Airways ATC approval via AirShare (or an observer in uncontrolled airspace). Shielded operations are an alternative.

source.publisher: Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand

entries.name: Taiwan (drone zones around airports)
entries.summary: Civil Aviation Act art. 99-13: no drone activity in the zone formed by 5 km arcs (35° each side) from runway-end centres and 2.6 km either side of the centreline; in the wider 10 km x 3.4 km extension, no drone activity from 200 ft (60 m) up (varies by airport); 1 km radius around airfields. Local governments may designate further zones below 400 ft.

entries.name: Hong Kong (small unmanned aircraft rules)
entries.summary: Small Unmanned Aircraft Order (Cap. 448G): risk-based rules (registration of drones and remote pilots except A1 operations of 250 g or less, training, insurance); no flying in Restricted Flying Zones shown on CAD's Drone Map unless wholly enclosed, nor over the Penny's Bay prohibition area; higher-risk 'Advanced Operations' need CAD permission.

entries.name: PSAT/NMSQT (College Board)
entries.summary: Students may not bring or access during breaks: phones, smartwatches, smart glasses or any eyewear that provides access to the internet or to any AI feature or service, wearables, cameras, recording or listening devices.

entries.name: SAT School Day (College Board)
entries.summary: Students may not bring or access during breaks: phones, smartwatches, smart glasses or any eyewear that provides access to the internet or to any AI feature or service, wearables, cameras, recording or listening devices.
